question: Hádanka: Hlas takmer nemám, tak sa dorozumievam klepotaním zobáka. Keď je horúco, kakám si na nohy, aby som sa schladil. A vraj nosím deti. Kto som?
source_excerpt: Storks frequently excrete onto their legs to prevent overheating, a phenomenon known as urohidrosis.

extra.why_interesting: Everyone in Slovakia knows the stork on the chimney, but almost nobody knows it is practically mute or that it cools itself in a rather undignified way. The player solves it easily and laughs at the second clue.
extra.verification_notes: Storks use urohidrosis (excreting on their legs to cool), are largely voiceless and bill-clatter, and are the folklore baby-bringers; no newer developments invalidate this (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urohidrosis).

explanation: Dospelý bocian biely takmer nevydá hlas, a preto klepoce zobákom. Trus na nohách sa v horúčave odparuje a chladí ho ako pot.

question: Čo by ste našli, keby ste vianočnému kaprovi nazreli hlboko do hrdla?
source_excerpt: dental formula 1,1,3/3,1,1; teeth on the inner sides and look molar-like (pharyngeal teeth)

extra.why_interesting: Nearly every Slovak family has met the Christmas carp, often swimming in the bathtub. The idea that it hides teeth deep in its throat is a genuine surprise, and players can still work it out because a fish that eats snails and seeds must crush them somewhere.
extra.verification_notes: Common carp have no jaw teeth but have molar-like pharyngeal teeth in the throat, so 'Zuby' is correct (https://www.fao.org/4/AC233E/AC233E01.htm).

explanation: Kapor nemá v papuli ani jeden zub, ale v hrdle má hltanové zuby. Nimi rozdrví aj ulitky slimákov a tvrdé semená.

question: Pravda alebo nepravda: Keď ježko zacíti nový silný pach, začne si robiť penu zo slín a natiera si ju jazykom na pichliače.
source_excerpt: The entire process can last anywhere from just a few minutes to even a couple of hours.

extra.why_interesting: The claim sounds made up, which tempts players to answer 'false', but it is true. The hedgehog in a Slovak garden suddenly seems far odder than anyone thought.
extra.verification_notes: Self-anointing is well documented: hedgehogs meeting a novel strong smell or taste make frothy saliva and spread it on their spines (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Self-anointing_in_animals).

explanation: Pravda. Vedci to volajú samonatieranie a dodnes presne nevedia, prečo to ježkovia robia. Môže to byť maskovanie pachu alebo ochrana pred predátormi.

question: Na dvore chytíte sliepku, jemne ju pritlačíte k zemi a od jej zobáka nakreslíte kriedou rovnú čiaru. Čo urobí sliepka, keď ju pustíte?
source_excerpt: The chicken is in a state of tonic immobility, remaining still for anywhere from 30 seconds to 30 minutes.

extra.why_interesting: Players expect a released hen to run off cackling. Instead it lies frozen and stares at the line, as if hypnotised. Many Slovaks have seen hens in a village yard, so they have a way in, and the answer is a comic picture they can reach by guessing that 'something odd happens'.
extra.verification_notes: Chicken hypnotism (tonic immobility) leaves the chicken motionless for a time after release; the chalk line is a folk element that doesn't change the outcome (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicken_hypnotism).

explanation: Sliepka strnie, akoby bola zhypnotizovaná, a môže tak ležať od pár sekúnd až po niekoľko minút. Tento 'zázračný pokus' opísali učenci už v 17. storočí.
